subject: Termination notice window alternatives & clean termination language (MSA + Order Form)
messages:
From: Jordan Mills <jordan.mills@cloudoptix.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@cloudoptix.com>, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 09 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Term notice window & auto-renew language - MSA/Order Form

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the draft MSA and order form. Procurement at CloudOptix reviewed sections on term and auto-renew and we have two items we'd like to propose for negotiation before we proceed to signature: 1) shorten the auto-renew notice window from 60 days to 30 days, and 2) add an explicit 30-day termination-for-convenience right to the Order Form with limited liability carveouts.

We understand Redwood prefers longer notice windows for capacity planning; happy to explain our constraints in a quick call.

Attached is our annotated redline for the MSA (pdf) and a short summary of the ask. Would you be able to confirm who on your side is handling legal redlines so we can align?

Attachments: CloudOptix_MSA_comments.pdf (pdf stub), OrderForm_Termination_Request.xlsx (xlsx stub)

Thanks,
Jordan Mills\Head of Procurement\CloudOptix
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Mills <jordan.mills@cloudoptix.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 10:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Term notice window & auto-renew language - MSA/Order Form

Jordan —

Thanks for sending the annotated redline and summary. I'm the account owner and I'll coordinate on the commercial side; copying Dev (contracts) and Aditya (sales lead) so legal can take a look.

Quick responses to your two asks:
- Auto-renew notice window: we can propose a compromise of 45 days as a middle ground. Shortening to 30 days increases risk for capacity planning for committed pools (Dedicated customers) but for hosted customers this is more feasible.
- Termination-for-convenience on Order Form: Redwood typically reserves termination-for-convenience for limited circumstances and ties it to a pro-rated termination fee when committed capacity is reserved. For non-dedicated hosted accounts we can consider a 30-day termination with 30 days of paid notice equal to monthly commit.

I've attached a clean redline (MSA_v3_clean_redlines.docx) with two alternate options inline: Option A (45-day notice, pro-rate termination fee for dedicated), Option B (30-day notice, full-month termination fee regardless of capacity). Please review and let me know whether CloudOptix prefers Option A or B so legal can draft final language.

Can we set a 30-minute sync on Wednesday 13 May (10am PT)? If that works I'll send a calendar invite.

Thanks,
Irene Choi\Account Executive, Redwood Inference\irene_choi@redwood.com\(415) 555-0192

Attachments: MSA_v3_clean_redlines.docx (docx stub)
From: aditya_rao@redwood.com <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Jordan Mills <jordan.mills@cloudoptix.com>
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 13 May 2026 08:55:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Term notice window & auto-renew language - MSA/Order Form

Jordan / Irene —

Irene: thanks for the options. Jordan: from a commercial perspective, Aditya here — CloudOptix, our primary objective is to keep this moving to signature without introducing unpredictable exposure for Redwood. If you can accept Option A (45-day notice + pro-rated termination fee tied to reserved capacity), we can keep the committed capacity discount intact. Option B would force us to either remove the committed discount or increase price to protect capacity.

If you need, I can include a one-sentence commercial concession (shorter notice) in the order form in exchange for a 10% step-up on commit pricing for the first 3 months after termination. Happy to discuss on Wednesday.

Best,
Aditya Rao\Director of Sales, Redwood Inference\aditya_rao@redwood.com

Team / Jordan —

Quick legal read and recommended language below. Summary first, then proposed paragraph so Jordan/CloudOptix can see clean text to approve:

Summary:
- We can accommodate CloudOptix's request with Option A (45-day notice) without exposing Redwood to significant capacity risk if we include a limited termination fee tied to any active committed capacity on the order form.
- For hosted-only customers with no reserved capacity we are comfortable with 30-day notice but will retain standard auto-renew protections in the MSA.
- Termination-for-convenience: add a short Order Form clause allowing either party to terminate the Order Form for convenience with 30 days' notice, subject to payment of any pro-rated fees for committed capacity and a capped liability equal to three months' average charges.

Proposed Order Form clause (clean text):
"Termination for Convenience. Either party may terminate this Order Form for convenience upon providing thirty (30) days' prior written notice to the other party. If Customer has purchased dedicated or reserved capacity, Customer shall pay a pro‑rata termination charge equal to the unused portion of any committed fees for the remainder of the then‑current term, not to exceed three (3) months of recurring charges. Except for payment obligations under this section or for breach, neither party shall have further liability to the other in connection with a termination for convenience."

Proposed MSA auto-renew adjustment (clean text):
"Notice of Non-Renewal. Either party may elect not to renew the Agreement by delivering written notice at least forty-five (45) days prior to the end of the then-current term; provided, however, that for Customers without any reserved or dedicated commitments the notice period shall be thirty (30) days."

Action items:
- Jordan / CloudOptix: please confirm whether you can accept the 45-day compromise for accounts with reserved capacity, and whether CloudOptix wants the hosted-only exception to be applied to your order form.
- Aditya / Irene: if approved commercially, I'll incorporate the clauses into the final MSA/Order Form redline and produce a PDF for signature routing.

I'll attach a short PDF (Termination_Summary_20260512.pdf) with these clauses inserted for easier review.

Regards,
Marissa Cole\Senior Counsel, Contracts\Redwood Inference\marissa_cole@redwood.com
(415) 555-0140
